Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
732 PM EDT Mon Sep 14 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 240 PM EDT Monday...

A Frost Advisory has been issued for parts of the Adirondacks
and Northeast Kingdom for tonight.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 240 PM EDT Monday...

1. Dry and seasonable before a few showers possible Thursday.

2. Cool weather expected this weekend, with mainly dry weather 
up until a warm front approaches later in the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 240 PM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure will center overhead tonight, leading to 
efficient radiational cooling. Temperatures will drop into the 40s 
and 30s away from the shores of Lake Champlain. Patchy frost is 
expected in the colder hollows of the Adirondacks and Northeast 
Kingdom. As the high pushes off to the east tomorrow, warm air 
advection will moderate the airmass. Therefore, highs will mostly be 
in the 70s for the next couple days, with lows in the 40s and 50s 
and no threats of frost. It's a great stretch of September weather 
in store. An area of rain will attempt to move into the region on 
Thursday into Thursday night as isentropic lift occurs on a warm 
front. EPS members generally favor a wetter and farther north front 
while GEFS and CMCE members generally keep the rain to the south. 
However, any precipitation would be light and stratiform, with the 
wet EPS probabilities of a half inch of rain generally ranging 
between 10-20 percent.

KEY MESSAGE 2: After Thursday's precipitation, ~1025mb surface high 
pressure will shift east across Quebec Province. Any showers will 
come to an end overnight, and allow for a gorgeous a Friday. High 
temperatures will top out in the upper 60s to mid 70s with a steady 
north breeze. Some high clouds will begin to stream overhead, and 
that should keep overnight lows mostly in the 40s to lower 50s in 
the broad valleys Friday night.

For Saturday, a warm front will be approaching. So plenty of high 
level clouds will be overhead. This will keep temperatures tamped 
down. Given the extended timeframe, models diverge on how quickly 
precipitation arrives. Channeled flow aloft will be a fast, 100-120 
knots at 250mb just to our north are fairly fast. Cluster analysis 
on the LREF depicts more uncertainty on low to mid level zonal flow. 
The members with faster 700mb flow feature an earlier arrival of 
precipitation with the greater moisture fluxes. Tracking rain 
through panels of individual ensemble members, there are a handful 
that are very late with the arrival of rain well into Sunday. Will 
also note that there are some members with a solid swath of rain. 
Digging through NBM probabilities, there's about a 30-40% chance of 
1+ inch of rain and a 10-25% chance of 2+ inches of rain focused 
near or over the region Saturday into Sunday. The temperature 
forecast will be highly dependent on whether the warm front lifts 
north of the region or not. If it doesn't, then we'll likely 
continue to see 60s to near 70, and if it does, then we could see 
temperatures on the warmer side.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Through 00Z Wednesday...Mainly VFR conditions expected for the
next 24 hours as high pressure settles over the region. The only
exception will be a period of early morning valley fog, roughly
06z-13z. The most likely sites to see IFR/LIFR in fog will be
MPV/EFK/SLK, but it can't be ruled out at any terminal. Have
gone with 1/2SM in FG at the aforementioned terminals where
confidence is highest, with 3-6SM in BR with VCFG at all other
sites. SKC skies tonight give way to increasing mid/high level
clouds during the daylight hours Tuesday. Otherwise, light 
terrain driven winds overnight will turn towards S at 5-10 kt 
after 14z Tue.
